fields.name: Strategy & Geopolitics
fields.summary: AI is now treated as strategic infrastructure: chip controls swing between easing and tightening, states fund sovereign compute, militaries go AI-first, and power grids become the binding constraint.

regions.name: Compute, chips & export controls
regions.summary: US rules on Nvidia sales to China loosened for H200 in early 2026 then tightened on offshore subsidiaries; Blackwell stays banned and actual China sales have stalled.

landmarks.name: US conditionally allows Nvidia H200 sales to China
landmarks.summary: Commerce opened H200 exports under conditions, following a December 2025 deal giving the US government a 25% cut; the most advanced chips remain blocked.

landmarks.name: Export enforcer: zero H200s sold to China
landmarks.summary: A Commerce official told Congress no H200s had shipped, as Beijing reportedly urged firms to pause purchases and favour domestic chips.

landmarks.name: BIS closes offshore subsidiary loophole
landmarks.summary: New guidance blocks exports of top chips such as Blackwell to subsidiaries of Chinese companies located outside China, clarifying license rules in place since 2023.

regions.name: US-China competition
regions.summary: China is building a domestic AI stack on Huawei Ascend chips and open models while US-China summitry produced stability but no settlement on chips or rare earths.

landmarks.name: DeepSeek V4 runs on Huawei Ascend
landmarks.summary: DeepSeek released V4-Pro and V4-Flash open weights with day-zero support on Huawei, Cambricon and other Chinese chips, a test of China's domestic hardware stack.

landmarks.name: Trump-Xi Beijing summit
landmarks.summary: The May 14-15 summit extended the trade truce but left AI chip exports and rare-earth supply unresolved, per most analyses.

landmarks.name: China's 15th Five-Year Plan elevates AI+
landmarks.summary: Adopted in March 2026, the plan mentions AI 52 times and makes the AI+ integration initiative and chip self-reliance top national priorities.

regions.name: National AI strategies & sovereign AI
regions.summary: Governments from Canada and the UK to the Gulf and EU are funding domestic compute and models to reduce dependence on foreign providers, often through deals with US chipmakers.

landmarks.name: Canada's 'AI for All' strategy
landmarks.summary: Canada's national AI strategy commits over C$2bn, with a sovereign AI foundation as one of six pillars, after a sovereign compute strategy in April.

landmarks.name: EU AI gigafactories tender
landmarks.summary: The EU is procuring up to seven AI gigafactories backed by about EUR 10bn in public funds; bids close 12 November 2026 with awards expected in early 2027.

landmarks.name: Saudi Humain expands Nvidia deal
landmarks.summary: PIF-owned Humain expanded its Nvidia agreement as it targets about 3GW of data centre capacity by 2030, part of a Gulf push alongside Stargate UAE.

landmarks.name: US Genesis Mission for AI in science
landmarks.summary: Executive Order 14363 directs DOE and the national labs to build a shared AI platform for scientific discovery, with 2026 deadlines for an initial capability.

regions.name: International governance & safety institutes
regions.summary: Global AI governance has shifted to broad, nonbinding forums: the India summit, a new UN scientific panel and dialogue, and an annual international safety science report.

landmarks.name: International AI Safety Report 2026
landmarks.summary: Chaired by Yoshua Bengio with 100+ experts, the second report finds fast capability gains and uneven, underdeveloped risk management practices.

landmarks.name: New Delhi Declaration at AI Impact Summit
landmarks.summary: About 88 to 91 countries and organisations adopted a nonbinding declaration on inclusive AI; frontier firms signed voluntary commitments critics called weak on safety.

landmarks.name: First UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance
landmarks.summary: All UN member states met in Geneva on 6-7 July, alongside the UN Scientific Panel on AI's first preliminary report; the next session is in New York in May 2027.

regions.name: Defense & military AI
regions.summary: The Pentagon declared an AI-first strategy and clashed with Anthropic over usage limits, while Ukraine scales AI-assisted drones and ground robots with humans still approving strikes.

landmarks.name: Pentagon AI Acceleration Strategy
landmarks.summary: Hegseth's memo aims for an 'AI-first warfighting force', sets seven pace-setting projects and requires frontier models reach warfighters within 30 days of release.

landmarks.name: Pentagon labels Anthropic a supply chain risk
landmarks.summary: After Anthropic refused to drop bans on autonomous weapons and mass surveillance, DoD designated it a risk; a district court ruled the move arbitrary in August.

landmarks.name: Ukraine bets on battlefield AI
landmarks.summary: Ukraine's Defense AI Center coordinates 2,000+ firms and reports 70+ AI and vision systems at the front, while officials say full autonomy is years away.

regions.name: Energy & data centres
regions.summary: Gigawatt-scale AI campuses are coming online and data centre power use is rising about a quarter a year, pushing hyperscalers into nuclear deals and straining local grids like PJM.

landmarks.name: Gartner: data centre power up 26% in 2026
landmarks.summary: Gartner forecasts global data centre electricity use of 565TWh in 2026, up from 447TWh in 2025, driven by AI-optimised servers.

landmarks.name: Meta signs up to 6.6GW of nuclear power
landmarks.summary: Deals with Vistra, TerraPower and Oklo cover existing plants and new advanced reactors, the largest tech-nuclear commitment so far, with most capacity due by 2035.

landmarks.name: Data centres projected at a fifth of US power
landmarks.summary: Bloomberg reporting projects data centres could reach about 20% of US electricity use by 2035, intensifying fights over grid costs and capacity.

regions.name: Elections & information integrity
regions.summary: The 2026 US midterms saw widespread AI-generated political ads, mostly without disclaimers, plus foreign influence operations; rules are a patchwork of state disclosure laws.

landmarks.name: AI deepfake ads in US midterms
landmarks.summary: A multimillion-dollar wave of AI-generated political ads ran in 2026 races; the Wesleyan Media Project found only 27% carried an AI disclaimer.

landmarks.name: OECD logs midterm deepfakes as realised harm
landmarks.summary: The OECD AI incident monitor recorded AI deepfakes used to mislead voters in 2026 US campaigns.

landmarks.name: Voters turn to chatbots for election info
landmarks.summary: A Pew survey found 8% of US adults used chatbots for 2026 election information, raising questions about accuracy and persuasion.

regions.name: Open vs closed models
regions.summary: Chinese labs now lead open-weight models on usage and benchmarks, while Meta moved its frontier work to a closed model, leaving OpenAI's gpt-oss as a main US open option.

landmarks.name: Meta launches closed Muse Spark
landmarks.summary: Meta's first closed frontier model ships with no public weights, a break from its Llama open-weights strategy.

landmarks.name: Chinese models dominate open-weight usage
landmarks.summary: Analyses of OpenRouter data put Chinese open-weight models at roughly 61% of routed tokens by May 2026, led by Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi.

landmarks.name: MIT Tech Review on China's open-source lead
landmarks.summary: Reporting examines how Chinese open models overtook US ones in downloads and why US policymakers now see open weights as a strategic issue.

regions.name: Domestic AI regulation
regions.summary: The EU delayed AI Act high-risk rules to 2027-28 via a digital omnibus, and the US White House moved to preempt state AI laws through litigation and funding conditions.

landmarks.name: EU agrees AI Act omnibus delay
landmarks.summary: Provisional deal moves high-risk obligations to December 2027 and August 2028 and adds a ban on nudification apps.

landmarks.name: US order targets state AI laws
landmarks.summary: A December 2025 executive order created a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, formed in January 2026, and tied broadband funds to state AI rules; its legality is contested.
